summary: Two hard failures make the feature unusable as submitted: the new module imports a nonexistent `cosmos_approval` module on startup, and both `accept()` and `reject()` import an undefined `assert_pen` symbol from `cosmos_ccr`. There is also a state-machine bug where reproposing the same content-addressed SHA resets it to `PROPOSED`, defeating the intended one-decision-per-SHA behavior.
Two hardline-policy bypasses are present: path traversal escapes the `_delme` delete exception, and `http` exfiltration of key material is not recognized as HARDLINE.

The new module captures delegation facts in the ledger, but the key limits are not actually enforced on child execution, and there are two concurrency bugs around reservation/grant timing. `sweep_stale()` also has broader side effects than its API suggests.
The recall index is not yet safe to ship: it currently indexes conversation records that the authoritative convo fold would reject, and its rebuild hash does not cover all stored session fields.

The new file is close, but the PR is incomplete and currently misreports some failure modes: the recall standup is not wired into the existing own-clocks dispatcher, `--standup` exits successfully on elevation refusal, and the `--once` path leaves several expected setup/ledger failures uncaught.
The new module has a real atomicity bug around `prev_action_sha`, plus two verification-path gaps: GET refusal handling is incomplete, and SoD is only enforced on write, not on verification.
